key_insight: Zatom-2 is a unified atomistic generative foundation model that pretrains on both molecular and material data to improve generation, prediction, and cross-domain transfer.
engineering_relevance: This matters for computational materials and molecular design because a single pretrained model can support structure generation, property prediction, and force-conditioned sampling across chemistry, materials, and biology.
method: Pretrained on ~5 million structures from OMol25 and OMat24
Uses a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching
Supports generation, structure prediction, and energy/force prediction with force conditioning
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved molecular distribution fidelity over Zatom-1, strong benchmark performance, controllable low- and high-force generation, and protein backbone designability rising from 67.8% to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.
watch_item: The model’s broad performance may depend on large-scale high-quality pretraining data, so transfer to new domains or low-data settings may still require careful finetuning and validation.
paper_title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
